**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination — total knee replacement (CPT 27447)**
**Member:** Cameron Grant
**Member ID:** W389332857
**Reference number:** POC-6A7FD5286D-45525
**Date of denial notice:** 2026-08-03
**Policy at issue:** Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026 — https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2026-04/Cigna_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replac%20Arthro_V1.0.2026_Eff08.04.2026_Pub04.20.2026.pdf

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing Cigna's denial of the total knee replacement (CPT 27447) requested for me by my orthopedic surgeon, Dr. Duval. I am asking the plan to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery.

The notice dated 2026-08-03 states that the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment before the requested surgery. I am writing because the records that were submitted do document that treatment, and because they line up with the plan's own published criteria in Cigna CMM-311 Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty V1.0.2026. Below I have quoted that policy and matched each quoted requirement to what is in my chart.

### The plan's criteria, and what my records show

**1. Non-surgical treatment**

The policy states:

> "Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months' duration"

My records show non-surgical management directed by my providers over a span considerably longer than three months, and its failure:

- **NSAIDs for 6 months**, with inadequate relief.
- **Corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08**, which gave approximately 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Supervised physical therapy**, focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from **2026-04-20 to 2026-06-15**, **16 visits completed**, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

Taken together, these are provider-directed treatments extending well past three months, and my symptoms did not resolve: as of the most recent documentation I have **9 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest**, I **cannot climb stairs without assistance**, and I **wake 3–4 times a night with pain**.

The policy also contains an exception:

> "Criteria exception: Provider-directed non-surgical management may be inappropriate. The medical record must clearly document why provider-directed non-surgical management is not appropriate."

I am not relying on that exception — I completed non-surgical management. I quote it only to show that the policy treats this requirement as one that the record can satisfy in more than one way, and my record satisfies it directly.

**2. Imaging findings**

The policy states:

> "Imaging or arthroscopic findings show EITHER of the following:"

and, within that section:

> "severe unicompartmental (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral), bicompartmental, or tricompartmental osteoarthritis as evidenced by ANY of the following:"

> "Kellgren-Lawrence Grade III or IV radiographic findings"

My **weight-bearing knee radiographs dated 2026-06-19** show **bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing**, read as **Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4**. That is a direct match to the grade the plan itself names. My physical exam also documents **varus alignment, crepitus and effusion, and range of motion of 5 to 100 degrees**.

**3. Symptoms**

The policy states:

> "Symptoms include BOTH of the following:"

> "function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than one-quarter mile, limiting activity to two [2] city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration"

> "loss of knee function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment"

My pain has been present and progressive for **9 months** and is not relieved by rest, which is longer than the three-month duration the policy describes. On loss of function, my records document that I **cannot climb stairs without assistance** and that pain **wakes me 3–4 times nightly** — limitations that interfere directly with ordinary daily activities. If the reviewer needs my specific walking tolerance stated in distance terms, that measurement is here: [maximum walking distance before pain forces me to stop, per my treating provider's note].

**4. Preoperative optimization**

The policy notes:

> "Note: It is incumbent on the surgeon to preoperatively optimize reasonably modifiable medical and behavioral health comorbidities."

My records document **no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoking status**.

### A request about the criteria that were applied

Several of the provisions above end in a colon and introduce lists of further conditions that I was not able to obtain in full. The policy also contains other pathways, including language about "Imaging shows a fracture of the distal femur (trochlea, condyles)." and "Conservative management or surgical fixation is not considered a reasonable option." — provisions that describe a different clinical situation than mine. Because the denial notice does not identify which specific criterion my records were found not to meet, I am asking Cigna to state, in its appeal response, the exact criterion and the exact language it applied, so that I and my surgeon can respond to it precisely.

### What I am asking for

I ask that Cigna overturn the denial dated 2026-08-03 (reference POC-6A7FD5286D-45525) and authorize CPT 27447. My surgeon, Dr. Duval, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary for me, and the submitted records address the plan's own published requirements point by point.

I understand this appeal must be received by **2027-01-30**, which is 180 days from the date of the denial notice. I am submitting it through my plan's appeal process — online at my.cigna.com, or to the appeal address printed on my denial letter — and I can be reached by phone at the number below, or through Cigna at 1-800-244-6224, if anything further is needed.

Please let me know in writing what additional documentation, if any, would help complete this review. I am glad to have my surgeon's office send records directly.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Cameron Grant**
